To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have proposed a new method to construct preconditioners of parameter-dependent matrices, and we have shown how to use this method to improve the efficiency and the accuracy of projection-based model order reduction methods for parameter-dependent problems.

we propose a method for preconditioning of parameter dependent matrices based on interpolation of inverse matrices and that we introduce strategies for adaptive selection of interpolation nodes in order to obtain optimal preconditioners for different objectives.

the Frobenius-norm-based interpolation of inverse operators can be applied in a variety of model reduction settings, and that it is possible to construct efficient preconditioners for large-scale parameter-dependent systems of equations.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of efficient preconditioning techniques for the solution of systems of parameter dependent partial differential equations, and with the improvement of the efficiency of projection based model reduction methods.
the development of a new class of model reduction methods that are based on the adaptive selection of parameter points and interpolation.

the construction and application of efficient preconditioners for the solution of parameter dependent linear systems of equations arising from the numerical solution of parameter dependent differential equations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed interpolation method is an effective and robust tool that can be used for a wide range of applications in the context of model order reduction.
the proposed method is a very powerful tool for the construction of efficient preconditioners.

, in the context of model order reduction, the use of random matrix techniques is a promising approach for the construction of efficient preconditioners for the solution of parameter dependent systems of equations, and that this approach can also be used in the context of sampling based model order methods.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a general method for the construction preconditioners of large parameter dependent matrices.

the interpolation of the inverse operator is an efficient method for the construction and reuse of preconditioners for the solution of parameter dependent equations in model order reduction methods and for the construction of residual based error estimates.
we propose a general framework for interpolation of inverse preconditioners for parameter dependent systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the construction of preconditioner based on the interpolation of the inverse is a powerful tool that can be used to construct preconditioners for a wide range of model reduction techniques.
the proposed interpolation of the inverse matrix can be used to construct preconditioners of large matrices that are parameter dependent.

interpolation of the matrix inversion is a viable strategy for the solution of parameter dependent systems, and that the proposed estimators can be used for adaptive selection of interpolation parameters in the context of model order reduction.
